Tuned vs iMPlayer

November 19, 2026

iMPlayer, from HzApps, is a modern player on Android and Apple devices, with Trakt, TMDB details and a Premium subscription. It's one of the closest apps to Tuned in spirit. Here is how they compare.

At a glance

iMPlayerTuned
Where it runsAndroid, Google TV, Fire TV, iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and MacAndroid phones, tablets, Chromebooks, Android TV and Google TV
Playlist typesM3U, Xtream Codes and Stalker portal (Stalker per a third-party review)Xtream Codes login, M3U link, M3U file, MAC portal (live TV and guide)
TV guideFull guide, with outside guide sourcesXMLTV guide as a list or a full grid, with reminders
Catch-upYesYes, on Xtream servers that keep recordings
RecordingYes (per a third-party review)Yes, the channel you are watching (Premium)
Pause and rewind live TVLocal timeshiftYes, up to an hour kept on the device (Premium)
Several channels at onceYes (on iPad on Apple devices)No, on purpose: one stream connection at a time
Casting to a TVChromecast (iOS)Chromecast
Picture-in-pictureYesYes
Offline downloadsNot stated by the developerFilms and episodes, whole seasons too (more than 3 at a time is Premium)
Profiles and parental controlsNot stated by the developerUp to 6 profiles, kids profiles and PINs (Premium); adult categories locked behind a PIN
TraktYes, and SimklYes, scrobbles films and episodes (Premium)
Film and show detailsTMDBTMDB ratings, trailers, cast and actor pages, saved on the device
SubtitlesCaption stylingFull caption styling, timing fix, and subtitle search for films and episodes
AdsNone reportedNone, ever
PricePremium subscription US$24.99 on the App StoreFree; Premium US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial, or US$24.99 once

"Not stated by the developer" means we couldn't find it on the developer's own pages or store listing. It may still be there, so check before you rule it out.

Price

iMPlayer is free to install, with a Premium subscription listed at US$24.99 on the App Store. A third-party review lists US$20 a year or US$35 for life, a 24-hour trial, up to five devices, and a free version limited to one playlist and live TV; we couldn't confirm those on the developer's own pages. Tuned's free version has no playlist limit on live TV, films and shows; Premium is US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial or US$24.99 once.

Tuned's prices are what Google Play charges in the United States; Play shows them in your own currency. Premium covers up to three devices, and a Tuned account can add more.

Where iMPlayer is ahead

  • Apple devices. iMPlayer runs on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV as well as Android.
  • Multi-view. Tuned keeps to one connection by design.

Where Tuned is ahead

  • Offline downloads of films, episodes and whole seasons.
  • Live events pulled from the guide, with Tune and alerts for teams you follow.
  • Profiles with kids profiles and PINs, up to six.
  • A cheaper yearly Premium, and a free version that isn't limited to live TV.

What Tuned does that most players don't

  • Opens straight to your channels. The playlist and guide live on the device, so the app shows channels the moment it opens and keeps them fresh in the background. Lists page straight from the database, so a playlist with tens of thousands of streams scrolls smoothly.
  • One stream connection, ever. The player, downloads, recordings, channel scans and backup copies take turns on a single connection, and anything in the background waits while you watch. Providers limit connections per account, and Tuned never uses a second one.
  • Live events from your guide. Today's games and fights are pulled out of the guide into one page. Tune finds a working English stream for an event, one channel at a time, and you can follow a team, league or fighter to get an alert before they play.
  • Backup copies and dead channels. When a channel has several copies, Tuned tries the next one if the first won't play, and a channel scan hides channels that never work, without blaming them for a slow internet connection or a busy server.
  • Real names over numbers. Episodes show their real titles from TMDB rather than "S1 E1", and tapping an actor opens everything they've been in, with what's in your playlist marked.
  • Sign in on a TV with your phone. Scan a QR code on the TV and type the login on your phone instead of with the remote.

Which one to pick

Both are modern and fast. If you also use an iPhone or Apple TV, iMPlayer covers them. If you're on Android and want downloads, live events and profiles, try Tuned.
